audit.why: Emerald+ 52.35% over 2363 games, matches the table.

audit.whatIsWrong: New Destiny is never mentioned, so the entry never tells the player that minions block Graves's auto-attacks outright.
audit.why: Kit text: "Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units." A single minion between Tahm Kench and Graves absorbs the entire shotgun blast. For an immobile tank facing a burst marksman this is the whole defensive answer to the lane, and it appears nowhere in early, mid, late, spikes, whys or wants.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2] and wants.foe[1] describe his damage as "double-barrel Q" and a generic "shotgun burst pattern" with no mention of the terrain interaction.
audit.why: End of the Line "detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain". In a side lane that means Graves gets his damage far earlier by bouncing the shell off the lane wall — the reason standing near the wall against Graves is much worse than standing in the open. The entry gives the player no way to see that coming.
audit.corrected: Terrain detonation now named in whys[2] and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells the player nine separate times to trade "on Quickdraw's cooldown" without ever giving the cooldown, and whys[1] implies it is a fixed timer.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s, but "Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown of this skill". Counting a flat 16 seconds against a Graves who is auto-attacking the wave gets you caught — the timer he actually has is much shorter. That refund is the reason the plan the entry sells keeps failing.
audit.corrected: The 16s rank-1 figure and the auto-attack refund added to whys[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says "his armor stacks from the dash make the trade math swing against you" without stating the condition.
audit.why: True Grit gives two stacks only "If Graves dashes towards an enemy champion". So it is specifically the engaging dash that buffs his resistances — a Quickdraw away from you does not. That tells the player exactly which dash to punish and which to ignore.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry credits Tahm Kench with "Abyssal Voyage" 1 time(s) and treats it as a global/roaming ultimate.
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage was removed in the Tahm Kench rework. The kit file lists W = Abyssal Dive and R = Devour; there is no global travel ability in the kit at all. Advice built on "use Abyssal Voyage to roam / reposition cross-map" tells the player to press a button that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Every reference re-pointed to Devour (R) or Abyssal Dive (W) as appropriate, with the surrounding advice rewritten so it describes what those abilities actually do.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry repeatedly sells a "Q-stun then Devour" chain as one combo.
audit.why: Riot's own text in the kit: An Acquired Taste — "At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion"; Tongue Lash — "If the champion already has 3 stacks of An Acquired Taste, they are stunned and the stacks are consumed." The stun and the swallow draw on the same three stacks, so a Q cast at 3 stacks stuns and destroys the resource Devour requires. The real sequence is to let Q land the THIRD stack (which does not stun) and then press R.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as: build to three, let Q apply the third stack, Devour immediately; a Q thrown at an enemy already on 3 stacks stuns but burns the swallow.

edits.before: Level 1 is yours on paper — Tongue Lash's range slows Graves before his Quickdraw armor stacks mean anything, letting you contest the first wave and accumulate An Acquired Taste stacks without walking into shotgun range. But the moment he hits level 2 and Quickdraw goes live, the lane inverts: his dash both closes and reopens distance in the same animation, meaning the three-stack stun setup you want requires him to walk into Q range without an escape — which he now has. Play levels 2 and 3 defensively: take the short trade to stack passive autos at safe range, then back off and let Thick Skin grey health regen the poke rather than burning E for small value.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours on paper — Tongue Lash's range slows Graves before his Quickdraw armor stacks mean anything, letting you contest the first wave and accumulate An Acquired Taste stacks without walking into shotgun range. But the moment he hits level 2 and Quickdraw goes live, the lane inverts: his dash both closes and reopens distance in the same animation, meaning the three-stack stun setup you want requires him to walk into Q range without an escape — which he now has. Play levels 2 and 3 behind the wave: New Destiny's four bullets cannot pass through units, so one minion between you eats his whole auto. Back off and let Thick Skin regen the poke rather than burning E.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are your first real control window. Graves has no extra tools between 4 and 5, and if you've been patient your wave is nudged toward your side — force him to walk up for CS right into Tongue Lash slow range, stack to 3, and commit the Q stun the instant Quickdraw is on cooldown. Never engage into a fresh Quickdraw: his armor stacks from the dash make the trade math swing against you immediately. At level 6 the math goes to coin-flip: your Devour removes him from the fight entirely, but his R is a point-blank burst that can chunk you hard mid-commit if he has Serrated Dirk timing on you — use Abyssal Voyage as a repositioning and pick threat, not a straight all-in button.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are your first real control window. Graves has no extra tools between 4 and 5, and if you've been patient your wave is nudged toward your side — force him to walk up for CS right into Tongue Lash slow range, stack to 3, and commit the Q stun the instant Quickdraw is on cooldown. Never engage into a fresh Quickdraw: dashing toward you grants two True Grit stacks, so your damage is at its lowest right after he closes. At level 6 the math goes to coin-flip: your Devour removes him from the fight entirely, but his R is a point-blank burst that can chunk you hard mid-commit if he has Serrated Dirk timing on you — hold Devour for the ally he ults, not as a straight all-in button of your own.

edits.before: Tongue Lash's range lets you slow Graves and contest the wave before his Quickdraw armor stacks matter — use it to farm safely and bully him off CS without overstepping.
edits.after: Tongue Lash's range lets you slow Graves and contest the wave before his Quickdraw armor stacks matter — stand behind a minion and his four-bullet auto cannot reach you.

edits.before: Both ultimates are online and the math is genuinely coin-flip: your Devour removes him from the fight, but his R delivers a point-blank burst that can one-shot you mid-swallow if he's ahead.
edits.after: Both ultimates are online and the math is genuinely coin-flip: your Devour removes him from the fight, but Collateral Damage is a 100s rank-1 nuke that can drop you mid-swallow if he's ahead.

edits.before: Quickdraw comes online and his burst pattern is live — he can dodge your Q skillshot and instantly re-engage for free, making the 3-stack stun setup nearly impossible on his terms.
edits.after: Quickdraw comes online and his burst pattern is live — hitting you with autos cuts its 16s cooldown, so he can dodge Tongue Lash and re-engage far sooner than the timer suggests.

edits.before: His full burst rotation at level 3 beats your still-developing pattern — Quickdraw into double-barrel Q into Smoke Screen creates a trade window you cannot safely answer without stacks already banked.
edits.after: His full burst rotation at level 3 beats your still-developing pattern — Quickdraw into an End of the Line bounced off the side wall, which detonates it early on terrain, is a window you cannot safely answer.

edits.before: Stack An Acquired Taste to 3 in safe short trades, then commit the Q stun only when Quickdraw is on cooldown
edits.after: Stack An Acquired Taste to 3 in safe short trades, then Devour on the third stack, only when Quickdraw is down

edits.before: Keep his range advantage and shotgun burst pattern active by never letting you close to 3-stack melee range freely
edits.after: Bounce End of the Line off side-lane walls so it detonates early, and never let you close to 3-stack range freely

edits.before: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — His dash + armor stacks. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Graves Quickdraw: matchup-defining — Dash + True Grit, 16s at rank 1, refunded by autos. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

notes: Two big absences here, both straight from Riot's own kit text: minions eat his entire auto (New Destiny bullets cannot pass through units), and End of the Line detonates on terrain so the side-lane wall is his friend, not yours. Also worth knowing that Quickdraw's cooldown is refunded by basic attacks — the entry told the player to count a timer that does not run at a fixed rate.
